en: floodplain strip between a river and its embankment
ex: In piena il Po invade le golene e allaga i pioppeti.
exEn: In spate the Po floods the embanked plains and submerges the poplar groves.
note: Hydrological/regional term of the Po valley; adj. 'golenale' (aree golenali). No exact English equivalent.

en: spring, upwelling of water; bubbling source
ex: Da una polla ai piedi della rupe sgorgava acqua limpidissima.
exEn: From a spring at the foot of the crag gushed crystal-clear water.
note: Literary/technical; 'polla sorgiva'. Not to be confused with 'pollo'.

en: resurgence spring (where groundwater re-emerges in the plain)
ex: La fascia delle risorgive tra Friuli e Veneto alimenta fiumi dall'acqua sempre fredda.
exEn: The belt of resurgence springs between Friuli and Veneto feeds rivers whose water is always cold.
note: Also 'fontanile' in Lombardy. Geographical term you meet in descriptions of the Pianura Padana.

ex: La barca fu risucchiata dal gorgo sotto la cascata.
exEn: The boat was sucked into the whirlpool beneath the waterfall.
note: Literary; figurative 'il gorgo della depressione'. Cf. 'vortice', 'mulinello' (smaller eddy).

en: broad torrent bed (dry most of the year), esp. in Calabria and Sicily
ex: Le fiumare calabresi restano asciutte per mesi e poi si gonfiano in poche ore.
exEn: The Calabrian torrent beds stay dry for months and then swell in a few hours.
note: Regional-geographical term of the South; in Reggio Calabria dialect also a place name. Cf. 'greto'.

ex: La pioggia trasformò il vialetto in una rete di rigagnoli fangosi.
exEn: The rain turned the driveway into a network of muddy rivulets.
note: Diminutive-pejorative of 'rigo'; also for sweat or blood running down: 'un rigagnolo di sangue'.

ex: La risacca trascinava i ciottoli con un lungo brontolio.
exEn: The backwash dragged the pebbles with a long rumbling.
note: The returning movement of a wave; often in the collocation 'il rumore della risacca'. Figurative in journalism: 'la risacca dei consensi'.

ex: C'è maretta nel partito dopo il voto sulla fiducia.
exEn: There is unrest in the party after the confidence vote.
note: Diminutive of 'mare'; in journalism almost always figurative ('c'è maretta tra i due alleati').

en: salt air; salt deposit (from sea spray)
ex: La salsedine aveva corroso le ringhiere di ferro del lungomare.
exEn: The salt air had corroded the iron railings along the seafront.
note: Uncountable; 'odore di salsedine'. From Latin salsus; not the same as 'salinità' (salinity).

ex: Il negoziato si è impantanato in un pantano di veti incrociati.
exEn: The negotiation has got bogged down in a morass of mutual vetoes.
note: Both literal (muddy ground) and figurative. Verb: impantanarsi. Adj. 'pantanoso'.

ex: L'eremita visse trent'anni in una spelonca sul monte.
exEn: The hermit lived thirty years in a cave on the mountain.
note: Literary and often pejorative ('una spelonca di ladri', from the Gospel). Neutral: 'grotta', 'caverna'. Root of 'speleologia'.

en: fumarole (volcanic vent of steam and gas)
ex: Alla Solfatara di Pozzuoli le fumarole sibilano tra un odore acre di zolfo.
exEn: At the Solfatara of Pozzuoli the fumaroles hiss amid an acrid smell of sulphur.
note: Volcanological term borrowed into English from Italian; cf. 'solfatara', 'mofeta' (CO2 vent).

ex: L'arsura di luglio aveva screpolato la terra dei campi.
exEn: July's parching heat had cracked the soil of the fields.
note: Literary, from 'ardere'; also physical thirst ('avere l'arsura'). Cf. 'calura', 'siccità' (drought, neutral).

ex: Le stelle del firmamento brillavano come mai in città.
exEn: The stars of the firmament shone as they never do in the city.
note: Literary/biblical; figurative 'una stella del firmamento cinematografico'. Everyday: 'cielo'.

ex: Un nembo nero avanzava da ovest oscurando la pianura.
exEn: A black storm cloud advanced from the west, darkening the plain.
note: Literary; in meteorology survives in 'cumulonembo', 'nembostrato'. Figurative 'un nembo di polvere' (a swirl of dust).

ex: Una saetta squarciò il cielo e il tuono seguì quasi subito.
exEn: A bolt of lightning tore the sky and the thunder followed almost at once.
note: Literary for 'fulmine'; 'correre come una saetta'. Also the 'saetta' is a clock hand in some dialects.

ex: Una landa desolata si stendeva a perdita d'occhio sotto il cielo plumbeo.
exEn: A desolate moor stretched as far as the eye could see under the leaden sky.
note: Literary; 'landa desolata' is a fixed collocation (also figurative for cultural wastelands).

ex: In quella plaga remota dell'Appennino non arrivava neppure la corriera.
exEn: In that remote stretch of the Apennines not even the country bus arrived.
note: Latinate and literary (Carducci, D'Annunzio); ironic in modern use. Not to be confused with 'piaga' (wound, plague).

ex: Le botteghe di Volterra lavorano l'alabastro da secoli.
exEn: The workshops of Volterra have been working alabaster for centuries.
note: Material; literary comparison 'pelle d'alabastro'. Adj. 'alabastrino'.

ex: I vigneti coprono il dolce declivio che scende verso il lago.
exEn: Vineyards cover the gentle slope that runs down to the lake.
note: Literary/geographical; the opposite is 'acclivio' (upward slope, rare). Everyday: 'pendio'.

ex: Con quelle scelte il governo si è messo su una brutta china.
exEn: With those choices the government has set itself on a dangerous downward path.
note: Literal sense literary; figurative 'essere/mettersi su una brutta china', 'risalire la china' (to recover). Homonym: 'china' = India ink, 'inchiostro di china'.

en: deep gorge, ravine (with a torrent); (adj.) horrid, dreadful
ex: L'Orrido di Bellano è una gola scavata dal torrente Pioverna nella roccia.
exEn: The Orrido di Bellano is a gorge carved by the Pioverna torrent into the rock.
note: As a noun, a specific type of dramatic ravine (Lombardy, Piedmont); as an adjective, literary for 'orribile'.

ex: Un capriolo sbucò dal bosco e attraversò la radura in tre balzi.
exEn: A roe deer came out of the wood and crossed the clearing in three bounds.
note: Smaller than 'cervo' (red deer) and 'daino' (fallow deer). Also 'capriola' = somersault (unrelated sense).

ex: Il gheppio restava sospeso nel vento, immobile, prima di piombare sulla preda.
exEn: The kestrel hung in the wind, motionless, before plunging on its prey.
note: Small falcon known for hovering ('fare lo spirito santo' in hunters' jargon). Cf. 'falco', 'poiana', 'nibbio'.

ex: Il nibbio reale si riconosce in volo dalla lunga coda forcuta.
exEn: The red kite is recognisable in flight by its long forked tail.
note: 'Nibbio reale' (red kite), 'nibbio bruno' (black kite). Leonardo recorded a childhood memory of a nibbio.

ex: L'allodola si alzava cantando sopra i campi di grano appena mietuti.
exEn: The skylark rose singing over the freshly reaped wheat fields.
note: Symbol of dawn and of the countryside in poetry; 'specchietto per le allodole' = a lure, a decoy (from hunting).

ex: Una cinciallegra beccava i semi di girasole sul davanzale.
exEn: A great tit was pecking at sunflower seeds on the windowsill.
note: Compound of 'cincia' (tit) + 'allegra'. Related: 'cinciarella' (blue tit), 'cincia mora' (coal tit).

ex: Le falene turbinavano attorno al lampione come impazzite.
exEn: The moths whirled around the streetlamp as if crazed.
note: Nocturnal lepidopteran; 'tarma' is the clothes moth. Figurative: attracted to danger 'come una falena alla fiamma'.

ex: Sullo stagno una libellula azzurra sfiorava l'acqua a scatti.
exEn: On the pond a blue dragonfly skimmed the water in jerks.
note: From Latin libella (a little balance), for its horizontal wings. Poetic image of lightness and summer.

ex: A maggio le pendici del Vesuvio si tingono del giallo delle ginestre.
exEn: In May the slopes of Vesuvius are dyed yellow with broom.
note: Leopardi's last great poem is 'La ginestra' (1836); symbol of resilience on barren ground. Not the same as 'ginepro' (juniper).

ex: Un doppio filare di cipressi conduce alla villa sul colle.
exEn: A double row of cypresses leads to the villa on the hill.
note: Emblem of the Tuscan landscape and of cemeteries (Carducci, Foscolo's 'Sepolcri'). Colloquially 'cipressi' evokes the graveyard.

ex: A giugno il profumo dei tigli in fiore invade i viali della città.
exEn: In June the scent of the lime trees in bloom fills the city's avenues.
note: 'Fiori di tiglio' for herbal tea; Proust's madeleine was dipped in 'infuso di tiglio'. Not the English 'lime' fruit (= 'lime').

ex: La faggeta d'autunno era un tripudio di rame e d'oro.
exEn: The beech wood in autumn was a riot of copper and gold.
note: 'Faggeta' = beech wood; 'faggiola' = beechnut. The high Apennines are covered in faggete.

ex: I salici piangenti si specchiavano nel canale.
exEn: The weeping willows were reflected in the canal.
note: 'Salice piangente' (weeping willow); Quasimodo: 'Alle fronde dei salici'. Aspirin derives from its bark (acido salicilico).

ex: Le foglie giovani di tarassaco si mangiano in insalata, amare e depurative.
exEn: Young dandelion leaves are eaten in salad, bitter and cleansing.
note: Learned/botanical name; popular names: 'dente di leone', 'soffione' (the seed head), 'piscialetto' (regional, jocular).

ex: L'upupa, con la sua cresta a ventaglio, è l'uccello più elegante dell'estate.
exEn: The hoopoe, with its fan-shaped crest, is the most elegant bird of summer.
note: Stressed on the first syllable: ÙPUPA. Foscolo made it a bird of ill omen in 'Dei Sepolcri'; Montale rehabilitated it.

ex: Una biscia d'acqua nuotava sinuosa tra le canne.
exEn: A water snake was swimming sinuously among the reeds.
note: Harmless, as opposed to 'vipera'. Colloquial: 'una strada a biscia' (winding road).

ex: La Dama con l'ermellino di Leonardo tiene in braccio l'animale come un simbolo di purezza.
exEn: Leonardo's Lady with an Ermine holds the animal as a symbol of purity.
note: Also the white winter fur used on royal and judicial robes ('toga con l'ermellino'). Symbol of purity in heraldry.

ex: D'estate i tafani tormentano i cavalli al pascolo.
exEn: In summer horseflies torment the horses at pasture.
note: Figurative: a persistent, annoying critic (Socrates as the 'tafano' of Athens). Cf. 'mosca cavallina'.

ex: Sono rimasto lì come un allocco senza sapere cosa rispondere.
exEn: I stood there like an idiot without knowing what to reply.
note: The figurative use ('restare come un allocco') is more frequent than the ornithological one. Verb: 'allocchire' (to be dumbfounded).

ex: In ottobre i larici ingialliscono e le valli alpine sembrano prendere fuoco.
exEn: In October the larches turn yellow and the Alpine valleys seem to catch fire.
note: The only deciduous conifer of the Alps; masculine despite -e. 'Lariceto' = larch wood.

ex: Sotto i lecci secolari del giardino la calura d'agosto si sopporta.
exEn: Under the ancient holm oaks of the garden the August heat is bearable.
note: Typical tree of the Mediterranean 'macchia'; 'lecceta' = holm-oak wood. Cf. 'quercia', 'rovere', 'sughera', 'cerro'.

ex: In Gallura le sughere scortecciate mostrano il tronco rosso come una ferita.
exEn: In Gallura the stripped cork oaks show their trunks red as a wound.
note: From 'sughero' (cork); also 'quercia da sughero'. Sardinia and Sicily are the main producers.

ex: Il miele di corbezzolo sardo è amaro e ricercatissimo.
exEn: Sardinian strawberry-tree honey is bitter and highly sought after.
note: Its red fruit, white flowers and green leaves made it a patriotic emblem in the Risorgimento. Interjection 'corbezzoli!' = good heavens! (dated).

ex: A Capodanno si appende un rametto di vischio sulla porta come augurio.
exEn: At New Year a sprig of mistletoe is hung over the door for good luck.
note: Also the birdlime once made from its berries; 'vischioso' = sticky, viscous.

en: couch grass; (fig.) weed, something that spreads uncontrollably
ex: La corruzione cresce come la gramigna: la strappi e ricompare.
exEn: Corruption grows like couch grass: you pull it up and it comes back.
note: Proverbial image of tenacity ('la gramigna non muore mai'). Also a type of short curly pasta.

en: summer mountain pasture; transfer of livestock to high pastures
ex: A giugno le mandrie salgono all'alpeggio e ne scendono a settembre.
exEn: In June the herds go up to the summer pastures and come down in September.
note: Alpine farming term (also 'malga' for the hut and pasture). Cheeses 'd'alpeggio' are prized.

ex: Il campo fu lasciato a maggese per un anno perché la terra riposasse.
exEn: The field was left fallow for a year so the soil could rest.
note: From 'maggio' (the month of the fallow ploughing). 'Lasciare a maggese' = to leave fallow (also figurative for ideas).

ex: I tratturi del Molise sono oggi percorsi da escursionisti più che da greggi.
exEn: The drove roads of Molise are now travelled by hikers more than by flocks.
note: Historical-geographical term of the southern Apennines; the 'Regio Tratturo' network dates from Aragonese times.

ex: I covoni ammucchiati nel campo aspettavano la trebbiatura.
exEn: The sheaves stacked in the field awaited threshing.
note: Augmentative of 'covo' in its old sense of bundle; image of pre-mechanised farming (Van Gogh's 'covoni').

ex: Giasone partì alla conquista del vello d'oro.
exEn: Jason set out to win the Golden Fleece.
note: Literary/technical; 'il vello d'oro' (Golden Fleece). Not 'velo' (veil) or 'pelo' (hair).

ex: Dal bozzolo del baco da seta si dipana un filo lungo oltre un chilometro.
exEn: From the silkworm's cocoon a thread over a kilometre long can be unwound.
note: Figurative 'chiudersi nel proprio bozzolo' = to withdraw into one's shell. Related: 'crisalide' (chrysalis).

ex: Sul far del vespro le campane chiamavano i contadini a casa.
exEn: As evening fell the bells called the peasants home.
note: Literary for 'sera'; liturgically the evening office ('i vespri'). Historically 'i Vespri siciliani' (1282 revolt). Adj. 'vespertino'.

ex: Nel crepuscolo i contorni delle case si confondevano con il cielo.
exEn: In the twilight the outlines of the houses merged with the sky.
note: Both dawn and dusk technically, but usually evening. Figurative 'il crepuscolo di un'epoca'; 'i crepuscolari' were early-20th-century poets. Adj. 'crepuscolare'.

ex: Nel meriggio assolato tacevano perfino le cicale.
exEn: In the sun-drenched noon even the cicadas fell silent.
note: Poetic (Montale: 'Meriggiare pallido e assorto'). Everyday: 'mezzogiorno'. 'Meriggiare' = to rest in the shade at midday.

ex: Vent'anni orsono questa valle era ancora coltivata a vite.
exEn: Twenty years ago this valley was still planted with vines.
note: Follows the time expression, like 'fa': 'molti anni orsono'. Also written 'or sono'. Solemn or jocularly archaic.

ex: Di rado un romanzo d'esordio riceve un'accoglienza così unanime.
exEn: Rarely does a debut novel receive such a unanimous reception.
note: Formal-literary alternative to 'raramente'; also 'ben di rado', 'non di rado' (not infrequently). From 'rado' (sparse).

en: first light of dawn; (pl.) beginnings, dawn (fig.)
ex: Agli albori del cinema i film duravano pochi minuti.
exEn: In the early days of cinema films lasted a few minutes.
note: The plural figurative 'agli albori di' is by far the most common use. Singular literary: 'il primo albore'.

en: sunset, the setting of the sun (literary); the west
ex: Il sole volgeva all'occaso e la pianura si tingeva di rosso.
exEn: The sun was sinking to its setting and the plain turned red.
note: Highly literary Latinism (Dante, Carducci); 'volgere all'occaso' also figurative = to decline. Cf. 'tramonto', 'ponente'.

ex: All'imbrunire i pipistrelli cominciano a volteggiare sopra il fiume.
exEn: At dusk the bats begin to wheel above the river.
note: Substantivised infinitive; also 'sull'imbrunire'. Literary-neutral, more evocative than 'al tramonto'. Cf. 'sul far della sera'.

ex: Il passaggio dall'evo antico al Medioevo non fu certo una frattura netta.
exEn: The passage from the ancient era to the Middle Ages was certainly no clean break.
note: Used almost exclusively in 'evo antico', 'Medioevo', 'evo moderno'; 'medievale/medioevale'. Latinate.

ex: Un bel dì vedremo levarsi un fil di fumo, canta Butterfly.
exEn: One fine day we shall see a thread of smoke rising, sings Butterfly.
note: From Latin dies; survives in 'buondì', 'un bel dì', 'notte e dì', 'a dì 5 marzo' (old dating), and in the weekday names (lunedì...). Written with the grave accent.

ex: Si alzava a un'ora antelucana per studiare prima del lavoro.
exEn: He got up at a pre-dawn hour to study before work.
note: Learned Latinism (ante lucem); 'ore antelucane', 'levata antelucana'. Slightly ironic in modern prose.

ex: La luce vespertina dorava le facciate del corso.
exEn: The evening light gilded the façades along the main street.
note: Literary; also 'messa vespertina' (evening Mass), 'edizione vespertina' (evening edition, dated). Cf. 'serale' (neutral), 'mattutino'.

ex: Le sue sempiterne lamentele sul tempo avevano stancato tutti.
exEn: His everlasting complaints about the weather had worn everyone out.
note: From Latin semper + aeternus; solemn in Dante, ironic in modern use ('la sempiterna questione'). Cf. 'perenne', 'perpetuo'.

ex: L'esiguità dei fondi costrinse a rinviare i lavori.
exEn: The scantiness of the funds forced the works to be postponed.
note: Formal-bureaucratic noun of 'esiguo'. Invariable plural (rarely used).

ex: L'incidente ha avuto cause plurime, tecniche e umane.
exEn: The accident had multiple causes, technical and human.
note: Formal-legal register ('omicidio plurimo', 'voto plurimo'); everyday 'molteplice', 'multiplo'.

ex: Una moltitudine di pellegrini gremiva la piazza fin dall'alba.
exEn: A multitude of pilgrims packed the square from dawn.
note: Elevated; 'la moltitudine' can also mean the masses (in political philosophy, e.g. Spinoza, Negri).

en: number, group, category (of things or people counted together)
ex: Il romanzo entra a pieno titolo nel novero dei classici del Novecento.
exEn: The novel fully belongs among the classics of the twentieth century.
note: Used almost only in 'nel novero di', 'entrare/rientrare nel novero', 'annoverare'. Formal.

ex: Una pletora di comitati e sottocommissioni rallenta ogni decisione.
exEn: A plethora of committees and subcommittees slows down every decision.
note: Learned (Greek medical term for excess of blood); always pejorative. Adj. 'pletorico' (bloated: un organico pletorico).

ex: Uno stuolo di fotografi lo attendeva all'uscita del tribunale.
exEn: A throng of photographers awaited him outside the courthouse.
note: Originally a military host (Greek stolos); today literary or ironic ('uno stuolo di ammiratrici').

ex: Ha commesso una caterva di errori nella traduzione.
exEn: He made a heap of mistakes in the translation.
note: From Latin caterva (troop); now colloquial-expressive, mildly negative. Cf. 'un sacco di' (informal), 'una marea di'.

ex: Il ministro ci sommerse con un profluvio di parole senza dire nulla.
exEn: The minister buried us under a torrent of words without saying anything.
note: Learned and ironic; 'un profluvio di lacrime/complimenti/cifre'. Literal sense (bodily discharge) is medical and rare.

ex: Il saggio è una congerie di citazioni senza un filo conduttore.
exEn: The essay is a jumble of quotations with no connecting thread.
note: Invariable Latinism, always pejorative (disordered accumulation). Cf. 'accozzaglia' (more colloquial).

en: handful, small group (of people); maniple (Roman military unit)
ex: Un manipolo di volontari tenne aperta la biblioteca durante lo sciopero.
exEn: A handful of volunteers kept the library open during the strike.
note: 'Uno sparuto manipolo' is a set collocation. Also the liturgical vestment. Cf. 'manciata' (handful of things).

ex: Le innumeri stelle del cielo d'agosto parevano a portata di mano.
exEn: The countless stars of the August sky seemed within reach.
note: Poetic variant of 'innumerevole' (D'Annunzio, Pascoli); also 'innumero'. Always plural in practice.

en: set of three; shortlist of three names
ex: La commissione ha proposto una terna di candidati per la direzione del museo.
exEn: The committee proposed a shortlist of three candidates to direct the museum.
note: Bureaucratic ('terna dei nomi'), mathematical ('terna pitagorica') and football ('terna arbitrale' = referee and two linesmen). Cf. 'terzetto', 'trio', 'triade'.

ex: Una poiana volteggiava in ampi cerchi sopra i campi appena arati.
exEn: A buzzard was circling in wide loops above the freshly ploughed fields.
note: The commonest large raptor in Italy; 'poiana' is also a Piaggio aircraft name. Cf. 'gheppio', 'nibbio', 'sparviero'.

ex: La ghiandaia nasconde le ghiande e così, dimenticandole, semina le querce.
exEn: The jay hides acorns and thus, forgetting them, sows the oaks.
note: From 'ghianda' (acorn). Noisy, colourful corvid; 'ghiandaia marina' is the roller.

ex: Un ramarro verde smeraldo prendeva il sole sul muretto a secco.
exEn: An emerald-green lizard was sunning itself on the dry-stone wall.
note: Much larger than a 'lucertola'; 'verde ramarro' as a colour. Folk belief holds it bites and never lets go.

ex: La donnola, minuscola e feroce, riesce a uccidere prede grandi il doppio di lei.
exEn: The weasel, tiny and ferocious, manages to kill prey twice its size.
note: Diminutive of 'donna' (a euphemism, as in many languages). Cf. 'faina', 'martora', 'ermellino'.

ex: Quell'agenzia è una sanguisuga: trattiene metà del compenso degli artisti.
exEn: That agency is a leech: it keeps half of the artists' fees.
note: Compound sangue + suggere. Medical leeches ('mignatte') were used until the 19th century; figurative sense is the common one.

en: sapling, young shoot; (fig.) scion, young offspring
ex: L'ultimo virgulto della dinastia si presentò alle elezioni a venticinque anni.
exEn: The latest scion of the dynasty stood for election at twenty-five.
note: Literary; the figurative 'virgulto di una famiglia' is often ironic. Botanical sense: 'un virgulto di quercia'.

en: in those days, once upon a time (Latin, often ironic)
ex: In illo tempore le lettere si scrivevano a mano e si aspettava la risposta per settimane.
exEn: Back in the day letters were written by hand and one waited weeks for a reply.
note: Latin phrase from the Gospel readings; today jocular for a distant, half-mythical past.

ex: La plurisecolare tradizione del Palio resiste a ogni tentativo di modernizzazione.
exEn: The centuries-old tradition of the Palio resists every attempt at modernisation.
note: Formal-journalistic; 'secolare' (centuries-old or secular), 'millenario', 'pluriennale' (of many years).

ex: Ci rivedremo posdomani, se il tempo lo permette.
exEn: We shall meet again the day after tomorrow, if the weather permits.
note: Rare variant of 'dopodomani'; also 'posdimani'. Cf. 'avantieri' (the day before yesterday).

ex: Avantieri è arrivata la lettera che aspettavo da mesi.
exEn: The day before yesterday the letter I had been waiting months for arrived.
note: Literary equivalent of 'l'altro ieri' / 'ieri l'altro'. Also 'avant'ieri'.

ex: Stamane il cielo era terso come dopo un temporale.
exEn: This morning the sky was as clear as after a storm.
note: Literary and Tuscan variant of 'stamattina'; also 'stamani'. Cf. 'stanotte', 'stasera'.

ex: È uscito or ora: se corri lo raggiungi ancora.
exEn: He has just this moment gone out: if you run you can still catch him.
note: Slightly literary; 'or' is the apocopated 'ora'. Related: 'orsono', 'or bene', 'or non è molto'.

en: once in a blue moon; very rarely
ex: Ci sentiamo ogni morte di papa, ma quando ci vediamo è come se non fosse passato un giorno.
exEn: We speak once in a blue moon, but when we meet it is as if not a day had passed.
note: Colloquial idiom, invariable; used with 'a' as well ('a ogni morte di papa'). Cf. 'di rado'.

ex: In vent'anni il valore dell'immobile è diventato il decuplo.
exEn: In twenty years the value of the property has increased tenfold.
note: Also a noun ('il decuplo'); series: doppio, triplo, quadruplo, quintuplo, decuplo, centuplo. Verb 'decuplicare'.

en: not one jot; not the slightest bit
ex: Il testo della legge non è cambiato di uno iota dopo mesi di dibattito.
exEn: The text of the law has not changed one jot after months of debate.
note: Iota is the smallest Greek letter (Matthew 5:18). Usually 'non cambiare/spostare di uno iota'. 'Iota' is masculine and invariable.

en: a hundredfold; a hundred times as much
ex: Chi lascia tutto per seguirlo riceverà il centuplo, promette il Vangelo.
exEn: Whoever leaves everything to follow him will receive a hundredfold, the Gospel promises.
note: Also a noun ('il centuplo'); learned-biblical flavour. Verb 'centuplicare'. Series: doppio, triplo, decuplo, centuplo.
